question: Is Brussels seeking to revise the Beneš, Bierut and AVNOJ decrees? Will the EU risk destabilising Central Europe over these decrees?

In the recent Hungarian parliamentary elections, as well as afterwards, the issue of the Beneš Decrees has come to the fore. The European Parliament, for example, intends to address it in a separate debate.

Somehow, amid this post-election enthusiasm over Péter Magyar’s rise to power, it is being forgotten that the Beneš Decrees, the Bierut Decrees and the AVNOJ Decrees were key acts in the post-war order of Europe after 1945 and no longer have any practical application today. In its foreign policy, the EU often emphasises stability and respect for historical agreements. 1.
Is the High Representative aware that these three sets of decrees represent a closed historical chapter that ensured post-war stability in Central and Eastern Europe?

Does the High Representative not consider that opening up discussions on the revision of these decrees poses a risk to the Union’s foreign policy, as it could destabilise the historical foundations of the European order in relation to third countries?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) The so-called Beneš, Bierut and the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia (AVNOJ) Decrees are historical acts undertaken by national authorities prior to accession to the EU in a very specific economic and social context. The Commission ensures the respect of EU law, within the remit of its competences.
